==English== {{rfc|en}} {{number box|en|2}} ===Etymology=== From earlier {{m|en|twise}}, from {{inh|en|enm|twies}}, {{m|enm|twiȝes}}, from {{inh|en|ang|twīġes||twice}}, from {{m|ang|twīwa}}, {{m|ang|twīġa}} {{gloss|"twice"; whence Middle English {{m|enm|twie||twice}}}} + {{m|ang|-es|pos=adverbial genitive ending}}. Related to {{cog|stq|twäie||twice}}, {{cog|gml|twiges}}, {{m|gml|twies||twice}}, {{cog|gmh|zwies||twice}}. Equivalent to {{af|en|twi-|t1=(in) two; both|-ce}}. Similarly constructed to the prefixes {{dbt|notext=1|nocat=1|en|bis-|dis-}}, borrowed from {{cog|ine}} cognates. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/twaɪs/|[tw̥aɪs]}} * {{audio|en|en-us-twice.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|aɪs|s=1}} ===Adverb=== {{en-adv|-}} # {{U|two}} [[time]]s. #: {{ux|en|You should brush your teeth '''twice''' a day.}} #: {{ux|en|No person shall be elected to the office of the President more than '''twice''', and no person who has held the office of President, or acted as President, for more than two years of a term to which some other person was elected President shall be elected to the office of the President more than once. ('''1947''', {{w|Twenty-second Amendment to the United States Constitution}}, Section 1)}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1824|author=w:Lord Byron|title=Don Juan|chapter=Canto the Thirteenth|chapterurl={{fullurl:s:en:Don Juan (Byron)/Canto the Thirteenth}}|passage=I've done with my tirade. The world was gone; / The '''twice''' two thousand, for whom earth was made, / Were vanish'd to be what they call alone}} #* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=5|passage=He could not be induced to remain permanently at Mohair because Miss Trevor was at Asquith, but he appropriated a Hempstead cart from the Mohair stables and made the trip sometimes '''twice''' in a day.}} #* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=John Malathronas|title=Which languages are easiest – and most difficult – for native English speakers to learn?|url=https://www.cnn.com/travel/article/learn-a-foreign-language-wellness|date=2021-04-25|passage=Malay is the lingua franca of several Southeast Asia countries and has been simplified by its use as a second language by non-native speakers.
For example, the Malay plural is formed by repeating a word '''twice''' – buku means book and buku-buku means books.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220322023413/https://www.cnn.com/travel/article/learn-a-foreign-language-wellness}} # {{lb|en|usually with "as"|of a specified quality}} Doubled in quantity, intensity, or degree. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1826|author=John Nicholson|publisher=H.C. Lea|title=The Operative Mechanic, and British Machinist: Being a Practical Display of the Manufactories and Mechanical Arts of the United Kingdom|volume=1|pageurl=http://books.google.com/books?id=TJUAAAAAMAAJ&dq=%22twice%20as%20slow%22&pg=PA78#v=onepage&q=%22twice%20as%20slow%22&f=false|page=78 |passage=Thus it appears that if the machine is turning '''twice''' as slow as before, there is more than '''twice''' the former quantity in the rising buckets; and more will be raised in a minute by the same expenditure of power.}} #* {{quote-book|en|title=Domesticated Trout: How to Breed and Grow Them|year=1896|edition=4th |page=304|author=Livingston Stone|pageurl=http://books.google.com/books?id=IPg-AAAAYAAJ&dq=inauthor%3A%22Livingston%20Stone%22&pg=PA304#v=onepage&q=%22thin%20as%20a%20shad%22&f=false |passage=You can't get anything thinner than a spring shad, unless you take a couple of them, when, of course, they will be '''twice''' as thin.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1995|title=Highly Qualified Women|author=Louise Corti; Heather Laurie; Shirley Dex |publisher=Great Britain.
